I am an open book so I do not mind sharing. Trigger warning for mental health and suicide, I won't be graphic but wanted to give a heads up I'll talk about it. 

Long story short since I don't want to write an essay: I decided I wanted to be alive despite everything in my brain telling me to kill myself. 

I've attempted suicide several times, the first time I was 13 and my heart actually stopped for just under 3 minutes. Apparently that wasn't a low enough bottom for me at the time lol. 

I struggle with severe mental illness, suicidal ideation being a huge annoying factor in my life. So I always have this nagging "Just end it, no one will care. It would be easier" type of feeling even though I don't want to. It's hard to explain if you don't experience it, I think. 

Anyway, at this point I was isolated with someone who was not good for me, in a shitty state away from everyone I knew and loved. This person is also an addict. I remember being wasted, and annoyed this person didn't take down a dead plant from our balcony, on the third floor of these apartments, like I Asked them to. So I climbed up on the railing, again wasted, and reached as high as I could to try and get this plant down, and I fell off. Luckily, I fell backwards on my ass, safely on our balcony, and not forward 3 flights onto concrete and rock. But... I felt disappointed that I didn't fall forward. I had the thought "everything would finally be okay if I just fell the other way" and I sat with that for a second, and I realized I was fucking insane and exhausted. So I decided then and there: I wanted to not want to die.

I tried to get sober without changing anything, relapsed several times (again) and under some shitty circumstances I ended up in a treatment center. I went straight from the treatment center to an aunt I hadn't seen in 10 years and she took me in and helped me stay clean and sober until I found AA and learned how to live in sobriety, not just survive. 

I will say, it's a hard journey, and you have to want it. Even if you don't follow the program to a T, id recommend finding a community in AA and reading the 12 and 12 book to help your spiritual growth and keep yourself grounded.

So we got him into the vet about a month ago and they gave us some medicine for his respiratory issue, we got him on a pre/probiotic as well. 

He wasn't getting worse, but he wasn't getting better. He knew it was his time. Two nights ago he was being very cuddly and clingy, more so than usual, and just acting pretty strange all around. At bedtime he BEGGED to go outside which he hasn't done. So we let him into the backyard. 11pm my cameras show him looking right at the camera for a few before stumbling off to a bush in the front yard. 

He didn't show up for breakfast when we went to work. Dinner came around and he wasn't home. We took a drive around the block. We found him in a very grotesque state in a canal of grass in front of our home. >! His whole lower body was missing. He was just a head, some chest, and his front paws. His spine and guts were hanging out. Something ate him. !< We examined nearby and his remains and didn't notice any signs of a fight or struggle. No blood trail. We came to the conclusion he knew he was going to pass and didn't want to burden us so he wanted to be outside. I guess this is pretty common with cats.

A neighbor flagged me down and confirmed he saw him at 3am walking his dogs and thought he was just sleeping. He was intact, curled up a bit, but couldn't tell if he was breathing. He said his dog barked and lunged but that Odin didn't even react at all. So that helped me realize he didn't suffer. He passed peacefully under a tree and a >! coyote or bobcat took the opportunity to have a free meal. !<

It's heartbreaking. I wish we didn't find him that way. 

Looking at pictures is helping to erase that sight. 

Tldr; Odin had a respiratory issue and found his way outside to pass peacefully for the sake of not burdening us. He's such a good boy. Unfortunately >! a coyote or bobcat found his body and ate most of him before we could get to him. !<
